newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton up on reports of export quota rise.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton up on reports of export quota rise.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Friday extended gains on reports that reports that the federal government had released a fresh export quota of 100,000 bales (170 kg each), dealers said.
Fresh mill buying was however dull.
Shortage of ready stock against dwindling arrivals at producing centres also aided the uptrend.
"The Indian government has allowed export of 100,000 bales for the local state-owned agency called Maharashtra Cotton Growers Federation," one broker said.
"Other such agencies are also demanding export quotas from the government," he said.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 10 rupees at 1,060/1,090 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned rose by 20 rupees at 1,850/1,900 rupees per maund and F-414 rose by 20/30 rupees at 2,060/2,090 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) moved up by 100 rupees at 14,300/14,900 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while wagad cotton lifted by 100/200 rupees at 13,200/13,300 rupees per candy.
